parts.problem_md: Describe and explain the energy mix of a country or area you have studied.
parts.solution_md:
Norway is a HIC (High Income Country) in northern Europe where 90% of electricity comes from hydropower** [KU]**. This is because Norway has many mountains and rivers, which are perfect for generating hydroelectric power **[KU].** Hydropower also makes up 65% of the total energy use** [KU].**

Norway also uses some fossil fuels, like oil and gas, but most of this is exported instead of used in the country** [KU].** Norway has 1% of the world’s gas reserves and 0.3% of oil reserves. Other renewables like wind and solar are growing. There are now 53 wind farms, with 36 more planned by 2030, including the world’s first floating wind farm** [KU]**. People in Oslo even get a 30% subsidy for installing solar panels at home.

Norway uses little coal and tries to reduce oil use by encouraging electric cars—66% of new car sales were electric in 2021 [**KU].** The energy mix is very sustainable, but hydropower can be affected by drought, like in 2022 when energy supply dropped **[KU].**

Overall, Norway’s energy mix is mainly renewable, reliable, and environmentally friendly

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word is '**explain**', which means that the answer needs to give reasons for the mix of energy sources used in Norway.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> This is a 'level of response' answer. Each point made in the answer does not equal a mark.
> 
> AO focus = AO1 [KU]
> 
> - A top-level 3 (7 mark) answer will use specific examples that demonstrate detailed, developed knowledge and understanding [KU] of one country's energy mix
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of how to respond to this question. Additional information that could be used in the answer includes:

> 
>   - Firewood/charcoal
>   - Fossil fuels – coal, oil, natural gas
>   - Nuclear power.

parts.problem_md:
Study Table 3.2, which shows four plans which a government is considering to provide future energy supplies.

![Table 3.2 outlines four energy plans: A, nuclear power; B, more wind turbines; C, offshore oil and gas; D, coal imports.](assets/001-table-3-2-outlines-four-energy-plans-a-nuclear-p.png)

Use plans B, C and D to choose the plan you think will be the most effective in providing future energy supplies.
parts.solution_md:
Plan B will be the most effective because wind energy is renewable** [1] **whereas oil, gas and coal will eventually run out **[d] ** Wind energy will create no atmospheric pollution **[1] **whereas  oil, gas and coal will pollute the atmosphere **[d] **. This means the contribution to global warming will also be reduced.** [1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> The command word is '**choose**' this means the answer needs to include valid reasons to support the point of view given. The answer must explain why it is the best option or the disadvantages of the other plans.
> 
> **Mark allocation**
> 
> - 1 mark for evaluation/judgement** [1]**
> - 1 mark for simple points **[1] **
> - 1 mark for a developed point **[d]**
> 
> Answers can be either:
> 
> - 4 simple points plus evaluation
> - 1 developed point plus 2 simple points plus evaluation
> - 2 points which are developed plus evaluation
> 
> **Common errors**
> 
> - Common errors where students lose marks include:
> 
>   - Not including judgement or evaluation within the answer
> 
> **Alternative content**
> 
> The answer above is just one example of a response to this question. Other information that could be used in the answer includes:
> 
> - **Plan C**
> 
>   - May not find gas or oil
>   - It is a long time from exploration to use
>   - Environmental problems e.g. oil spills
>   - Expense of exploration
>   - Reduced reliance on imports of oil/gas etc.
> - **Plan D**
> 
>   - Imports of coal will increase import costs/balance of trade deficit
>   - Imports could be cut off in time of conflict etc.
